summary: WASM viability result for SongCore — durable machine summary (archived 2026-09-01 from the WASM total-cost evaluation; raw tournament trees were pruned, git history preserves the detail)
method: Same SongCore capability intent rebuilt for a WASM target; same ABI exercised from native twin vs WAMR (interp + AOT), wasm3, Wasmtime, and Emscripten/V8 (node harness); PCM compared per fixture.

artifact_terminology.purpose: Size numbers below are NOT the same artifact. These definitions are normative; never quote one under another's name.
artifact_terminology.guest_module_only: the SongCore.wasm guest module by itself, no runtime (xz -9e unless stated)
artifact_terminology.aot_guest_module_only: the wamrc-compiled SongCore.aot guest by itself, replaces the .wasm module in AOT deployments
artifact_terminology.runtime_only: the host runner / embedded runtime binary without any guest
artifact_terminology.runtime_plus_guest_bundle: the shipping package total: runtime + guest module(s)

correctness.tolerance_policy: max_abs_delta 1e-6 on PCM-derived fields; WASM runtimes bit-identical to the WAMR anchor on every tolerance-allowed stream
correctness.conclusion: WASM implementations produced matching SongCore behavior (bit-identical modulo the declared float tolerance).

wamr_interpreter.note: interpreters carry a large runtime tax

wasm3_interpreter.note: interpreters carry a large runtime tax

bridge_tax.definition: PCM transfer cost / guest decode cost, per backend

shipping_xz9e.note: Every entry is a runtime_plus_guest_bundle (the deployment total), decomposed into runtime_only and guest module. Historical prose figures resolve as: 1.29 MB = guest_module_only (SongCore.wasm); 3.55 MB = aot_guest_module_only (SongCore.aot); 4.02 MB / 1.30 MB xz = the WAMR-AOT bundle (runtime + AOT guest), not a single artifact.

native.artifact_definition: runtime_plus_guest_bundle — single native binary, no separate runtime

wamr_aot.artifact_definition: runtime_plus_guest_bundle — the AOT guest replaces the .wasm module

conclusion: WASM is viable but native-first remains the default architecture: same capability definition rebuilds for WASM, and AOT/JIT close the performance gap, but the native artifact is smaller and carries no runtime tax.
